Differential expression and enrichment workflow

Source: vignettes/differential-enrichment-workflow.Rmd
differential-enrichment-workflow.Rmd

What you will do

  • Question: which genes distinguish cell states, and which pathways summarize those differences?
  • Input: All 1,000 cells in the bundled mouse pancreas object, with CellType labels. Cells are observational units for this marker example, not biological replicates.
  • Output: A complete marker table, over-representation and ranked enrichment results, diagnostic plots and reusable tables.
  • How to run: start a fresh R session and run the chunks in order. Printed tables and figures below are generated from that run; code-only alternatives are identified explicitly.

This article shows how to organize differential expression, marker visualization, and pathway enrichment in scop. The main distinction is between testing genes, summarizing gene sets, and interpreting enriched biological terms.

Use this workflow after cell identities and major covariates are stable. Differential expression is gene-level evidence. Enrichment is a summary of a gene list or ranked statistic against a named database. Keep those two evidence layers separate in the text of a report.

Before the first analysis chunk, install the extra packages in the same R library as SCOP. Use BiocManager for AnnotationDbi, org.Mm.eg.db, GO.db and clusterProfiler, and CRAN for shadowtext (used by the network plot). These setup commands are run once, outside the analysis render:

BiocManager::install(c("AnnotationDbi", "org.Mm.eg.db", "GO.db", "clusterProfiler"))
install.packages("shadowtext")

Prepare the Object 

library(scop)
set.seed(11)

data(pancreas_sub)
input_cells <- colnames(pancreas_sub)
pancreas_sub <- RunStandardWorkflow(pancreas_sub, assay = "RNA",
                                   seed = 11, cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(pancreas_sub), input_cells))
data.frame(cells = ncol(pancreas_sub), genes = nrow(pancreas_sub))
#>   cells genes
#> 1  1000 15998

table(pancreas_sub$CellType)
#> 
#>        Ductal     Endocrine  Ngn3-high-EP   Ngn3-low-EP Pre-endocrine 
#>           253           355           169            67           156

Run Differential Expression

RunDEtest() writes differential-expression tables under srt@tools. The default single-cell marker workflow is appropriate for exploratory marker finding. Use sample-aware or pseudobulk methods when biological replicates are part of the question.

pancreas_sub <- RunDEtest(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  fc.threshold = 1,
  only.pos = FALSE,
  assay = "RNA", layer = "data", test.use = "wilcox",
  max.cells.per.ident = Inf, min.pct = 0.1,
  p.adjust.method = "bonferroni", cores = 1, seed = 11
)

de <- pancreas_sub@tools$DEtest_CellType$AllMarkers_wilcox
stopifnot(nrow(de) > 0, all(c("gene", "group1", "avg_log2FC", "p_val_adj") %in% names(de)))
data.frame(rows = nrow(de), unique_genes = length(unique(de$gene)),
           contrasts = length(unique(de$group1)))
#>    rows unique_genes contrasts
#> 1 36764         8465         5
head(de)
#>           p_val avg_log2FC pct.1 pct.2     p_val_adj          gene group1
#> 1 7.287773e-130   3.679046 0.897 0.096 1.165898e-125         Cyr61 Ductal
#> 2 1.168267e-127   3.217619 0.937 0.118 1.868994e-123       Adamts1 Ductal
#> 3 2.900413e-120   2.956891 0.976 0.173 4.640081e-116         Anxa2 Ductal
#> 4 8.561291e-113   2.733121 0.949 0.147 1.369635e-108 1700011H14Rik Ductal
#> 5 2.559824e-108   2.764483 0.960 0.229 4.095207e-104         Bicc1 Ductal
#> 6 1.495170e-103   2.646007 0.905 0.147  2.391972e-99         Gsta3 Ductal
#>   group2 test_group_number
#> 1 others                 5
#> 2 others                 5
#> 3 others                 5
#> 4 others                 5
#> 5 others                 5
#> 6 others                 5
#>                                                test_group
#> 1 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine
#> 2 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine
#> 3 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine
#> 4 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine
#> 5 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine
#> 6 Ductal;Ngn3-high-EP;Endocrine;Ngn3-low-EP;Pre-endocrine

fc.threshold = 1 is a fold-change ratio of one (log2 cutoff zero), not a log2-fold-change cutoff of one. Both directions are retained, with no cell subsampling. The detection filter is 10% in at least one group and adjusted p-values use Bonferroni here. An adjusted p-value displayed as zero reflects numerical underflow, not certainty.

Keep the contrast, grouping column, test method, and threshold in the report. Those choices define the meaning of each marker table. For FindAllMarkers-style results, group1 names the group being compared against the remaining cells unless a specific contrast is stated.

Plot Differential Results

Use volcano, Manhattan, and ring views for different levels of detail. Volcano plots are useful for one group or contrast; Manhattan and ring plots are useful when scanning many groups.

In the first volcano view, the horizontal coordinate is the difference in detected-cell fractions (pct.1 - pct.2), not log-fold change. The vertical coordinate is signed significance: downregulated genes are drawn below zero; its magnitude is -log10(p_val_adj). Colour shows log2-fold change. The enrichment-annotated volcano below instead uses the conventional log2-fold change horizontal coordinate and unsigned significance.

DEtestPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  plot_type = "volcano",
  label.size = 2
)


DEtestPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  plot_type = "manhattan",
  label.size = 2
)


DEtestPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  plot_type = "ring",
  label.size = 2
)

Prepare a tested-gene GO background

Install the mouse annotation resources in advance (org.Mm.eg.db, GO.db and AnnotationDbi), clusterProfiler for GSEA and shadowtext for network labels. The native ORA backend does not need clusterProfiler. This chunk reads real, locally installed GO Biological Process annotations and records their versions. The common background contains only genes returned by every DE comparison, before significance filtering. This conservative shared universe avoids treating genes excluded from the tests as eligible negative results. No database downloads or invented pathway memberships occur during this step.

tested_by_group <- split(de$gene, de$group1)
measured_genes <- Reduce(intersect, tested_by_group)
stopifnot(length(measured_genes) > 0)
valid_symbols <- intersect(measured_genes,
                           AnnotationDbi::keys(org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db, keytype = "SYMBOL"))
go_map <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db,
                                keys = valid_symbols, keytype = "SYMBOL",
                                columns = c("GOALL", "ONTOLOGYALL"))
go_term2gene <- unique(go_map[!is.na(go_map$GOALL) & go_map$ONTOLOGYALL == "BP",
                               c("GOALL", "SYMBOL")])
colnames(go_term2gene) <- c("Term", "symbol")
go_term2name <- AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db::GO.db,
                                      keys = unique(go_term2gene$Term),
                                      keytype = "GOID", columns = "TERM")
go_term2name <- unique(go_term2name[stats::complete.cases(go_term2name), ])
colnames(go_term2name) <- c("Term", "Name")
go_version <- paste("org.Mm.eg.db", utils::packageVersion("org.Mm.eg.db"),
                     "; GO.db", utils::packageVersion("GO.db"))
stopifnot(nrow(go_term2gene) > 0)
data.frame(database = "GO_BP", version = go_version,
           genes_tested_in_every_group = length(measured_genes),
           GO_annotated_background = length(unique(go_term2gene$symbol)),
           terms = length(unique(go_term2gene$Term)))
#>   database                            version genes_tested_in_every_group
#> 1    GO_BP org.Mm.eg.db 3.23.0 ; GO.db 3.23.1                        6770
#>   GO_annotated_background terms
#> 1                    6109 11849

The ORA universe is the union of genes in this restricted GO mapping, not the whole genome. Genes outside the common tested set or without GO annotation cannot contribute. Because we supply TERM2GENE, SCOP stores the database key as custom; its biological source remains the versioned GO_BP mapping above. Keep that source information with the exported result.

When enrichment results are available, volcano plots can annotate enriched terms to connect marker genes with pathway-level interpretation. The enrichment overlay circles genes that belong to selected enriched terms. The legend title is the analysis layer (Enrichment), and the legend item is the database, here custom for the explicitly supplied GO_BP mapping.

pancreas_sub <- RunEnrichment(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  species = "Mus_musculus",
  TERM2GENE = go_term2gene, TERM2NAME = go_term2name,
  DE_threshold = "avg_log2FC > log2(1.5) & p_val_adj < 0.05"
)

DEtestPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  plot_type = "volcano",
  threshold_method = "hyperbolic",
  hyperbola_c = 6,
  annotate_enrichment = TRUE,
  enrich_from = "Enrichment",
  enrich_db = "custom",
  enrich_top_terms = 3,
  enrich_nlabel = 5,
  label.size = 2
)

Only five enrichment-associated gene labels per cell group are shown to keep the panels readable; the full marker and enrichment tables are exported. The dashed hyperbolic guide is a display selection rule, not an additional statistical test or the cutoff used to create the ORA input.

Summarize Markers in Heatmaps

Feature heatmaps are useful after markers have been filtered. Keep the filter explicit and avoid showing very large marker sets without grouping or splitting. The complete DE table is retained. Only the ten strongest positive markers per group are selected for this readable figure; this is a declared display choice, not a change to the test or its cell population. All cells remain in the plot.

DEGs <- pancreas_sub@tools$DEtest_CellType$AllMarkers_wilcox
DEGs <- DEGs[with(DEGs, avg_log2FC > 1 & p_val_adj < 0.05), ]

display_markers <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(DEGs, DEGs$group1), function(x) {
  head(x[order(x$avg_log2FC, decreasing = TRUE), ], 10)
}))
display_markers <- display_markers[!duplicated(display_markers$gene), ]
stopifnot(nrow(display_markers) > 0)

ht <- FeatureHeatmap(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  features = display_markers$gene,
  feature_split = display_markers$group1,
  max_cells = Inf,
  exp_legend_title = "Z-score",
  anno_terms = FALSE
)
print(ht$plot)

Run Over-Representation Analysis

RunEnrichment() tests whether filtered marker sets are enriched for terms from the selected database. GO_BP is Gene Ontology Biological Process. The specific enriched terms are the rows shown by EnrichmentPlot().

EnrichmentPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  db = "custom",
  group.by = "CellType",
  group_use = c("Ductal", "Endocrine"),
  plot_type = "bar"
)

Use different plot types for different questions: bar or lollipop plots for ranked terms, word clouds for broad themes, and networks or enrichmaps for term relationships. The exported table includes tested terms that did not pass adjusted p < 0.05; its row count is not a count of significant pathways. Related GO terms often share genes, so several similar terms are not independent biological findings.

EnrichmentPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  db = "custom",
  group.by = "CellType",
  group_use = "Ngn3-low-EP",
  plot_type = "network"
)


EnrichmentPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  db = "custom",
  group.by = "CellType",
  plot_type = "comparison",
  topTerm = 3
)

In the network, numbered circles refer to the GO terms in the legend; rectangles are genes and edges are annotation membership. This is not an inferred gene-regulatory network. Its axes are layout coordinates, not expression or pseudotime. In the comparison plot, dot size is GeneRatio and colour shows adjusted significance; use the exported table to distinguish nonsignificant terms from missing results.

Run GSEA

Use GSEA when ranked gene statistics are more appropriate than a hard marker cutoff. ORA depends on a marker cutoff, while GSEA uses a ranked gene list. Use GSEA when many genes shift modestly and a binary marker threshold would discard useful signal. This run ranks all finite tested log2-fold changes in both directions; it does not prefilter genes by significance. Positive NES supports enrichment toward the positive end of that group-versus-rest ranking, negative NES toward the other end. Statistical significance and effect direction must both be read from the real result table. GSEA performs substantial permutation work and can take longer than DE or plotting.

GSEA uses a separate GO mapping covering the union of the tested genes. Each group’s full ranking is retained. Reusing the ORA intersection would remove known GO memberships from genes that remain in a group’s ranking.

gsea_symbols <- intersect(unique(de$gene),
                          AnnotationDbi::keys(org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db, keytype = "SYMBOL"))
gsea_map <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db,
                                 keys = gsea_symbols, keytype = "SYMBOL",
                                 columns = c("GOALL", "ONTOLOGYALL"))
gsea_term2gene <- unique(gsea_map[!is.na(gsea_map$GOALL) & gsea_map$ONTOLOGYALL == "BP",
                                c("GOALL", "SYMBOL")])
colnames(gsea_term2gene) <- c("Term", "symbol")
gsea_term2name <- AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db::GO.db,
  keys = unique(gsea_term2gene$Term), keytype = "GOID", columns = "TERM")
gsea_term2name <- unique(gsea_term2name[stats::complete.cases(gsea_term2name), ])
colnames(gsea_term2name) <- c("Term", "Name")
stopifnot(all(go_term2gene$symbol %in% gsea_term2gene$symbol))
pancreas_sub <- RunGSEA(
  pancreas_sub,
  group.by = "CellType",
  species = "Mus_musculus",
  TERM2GENE = gsea_term2gene, TERM2NAME = gsea_term2name,
  DE_threshold = "is.finite(avg_log2FC)",
  nPermSimple = 10000,
  eps = 0
)

gsea_endocrine <- subset(
  pancreas_sub@tools$GSEA_CellType_wilcox$enrichment,
  Groups == "Endocrine" & Database == "custom"
)
gsea_id <- gsea_endocrine$ID[which.min(gsea_endocrine$p.adjust)]
print(head(gsea_endocrine[order(gsea_endocrine$p.adjust),
                         c("ID", "Description", "NES", "p.adjust")], 5))
#>              ID                                                   Description
#> 8228 GO:0009306                                             protein secretion
#> 8229 GO:0051046                                       regulation of secretion
#> 8230 GO:0035592 establishment of protein localization to extracellular region
#> 8231 GO:0071692                  protein localization to extracellular region
#> 8232 GO:0032940                                             secretion by cell
#>           NES     p.adjust
#> 8228 2.374474 7.275006e-12
#> 8229 2.194113 7.275006e-12
#> 8230 2.330899 7.531970e-12
#> 8231 2.330899 7.531970e-12
#> 8232 2.060459 7.531970e-12

print(GSEAPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  db = "custom",
  group.by = "CellType",
  group_use = "Endocrine",
  id_use = gsea_id
))


print(GSEAPlot(
  pancreas_sub,
  db = "custom",
  group.by = "CellType",
  group_use = "Endocrine",
  plot_type = "bar",
  direction = "both",
  topTerm = 10
))
#> Warning: `guide_colourbar()` cannot be used for alpha.
#> ℹ Use one of colour, color, or fill instead.

In the running-score plot, black ticks locate gene-set members in the ranked gene list; the green curve is the cumulative enrichment score. The lower panel is the log2-fold-change ranking statistic. The horizontal coordinate is a gene rank, not cell order or developmental time. Read the signed NES and adjusted p-value together with the term’s contributing genes.

Save, reload, and check the hand-off

The code below saves to a temporary directory. Choose a persistent output folder when saving your analysis. Save the object and plain-text metadata; a figure alone cannot reproduce the analysis. No cells are sampled for this export.

output_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "differential-enrichment-workflow")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
result_file <- file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds")
saveRDS(pancreas_sub, result_file)
utils::write.csv(de, file.path(output_dir, "all-markers.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(go_term2gene, file.path(output_dir, "GO-BP-measured-background.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(gsea_term2gene, file.path(output_dir, "GO-BP-GSEA-memberships.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(paste("GO_BP", go_version), file.path(output_dir, "GO-source.txt"))
utils::write.csv(pancreas_sub@tools$Enrichment_CellType_wilcox$enrichment,
                 file.path(output_dir, "ORA.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(pancreas_sub@tools$GSEA_CellType_wilcox$enrichment,
                 file.path(output_dir, "GSEA.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(pancreas_sub@meta.data, file.path(output_dir, "cell-metadata.csv"))
reloaded <- readRDS(result_file)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(reloaded), colnames(pancreas_sub)),
          identical(reloaded@meta.data, pancreas_sub@meta.data),
          identical(SeuratObject::Reductions(reloaded),
                    SeuratObject::Reductions(pancreas_sub)),
          identical(GetAssayData5(reloaded, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts"),
                    GetAssayData5(pancreas_sub, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")))
stopifnot(identical(reloaded@tools$DEtest_CellType$AllMarkers_wilcox, de),
          identical(reloaded@tools$Enrichment_CellType_wilcox$enrichment,
                    pancreas_sub@tools$Enrichment_CellType_wilcox$enrichment),
          identical(reloaded@tools$GSEA_CellType_wilcox$enrichment,
                    pancreas_sub@tools$GSEA_CellType_wilcox$enrichment))

Use your own data and recover common errors

  • Replace the data(...) input with readRDS("your-object.rds"), or create a Seurat object from a gene-by-cell raw-count matrix. Check that cell IDs are unique and metadata row names equal the expression column names.
  • Set the assay and grouping columns explicitly. Species, gene identifiers and reference labels must match your experiment; do not copy pancreas labels to unrelated tissue.
  • If a reduction or metadata column is missing, inspect SeuratObject::Reductions(object) and colnames(object@meta.data), then run its producer chunk. A plot does not create the result it needs.
  • If GO returns no terms, inspect gene identifiers, overlap, set-size filters and the actual adjusted p-values. Do not loosen thresholds merely to force a positive result. A valid empty result and an unavailable database are different.
  • If a dependency is unavailable, install it in the analysis environment, restart R and rerun from the input chunk. A skipped or failed method is not evidence that it worked. Preserve warnings and the exact error in your report.

Analysis provenance

The receipt records the R seed. Python methods retain their documented backend seeds and parameters; setting the R seed alone does not control every backend. Package versions, BLAS libraries and backend changes can alter numerical results. Keep this receipt with the exported object.

source_revision <- Sys.getenv("GITHUB_SHA")
if (!nzchar(source_revision) && nzchar(Sys.which("git"))) {
  source_revision <- tryCatch(system2("git", c("rev-parse", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE,
                                      stderr = FALSE)[1], error = function(e) NA_character_)
}
article_source <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
build_receipt <- data.frame(
  article = "differential-enrichment-workflow",
  built_utc = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
  scop = as.character(utils::packageVersion("scop")),
  R = as.character(getRversion()),
  source_revision = source_revision,
  source_has_local_changes = if (nzchar(Sys.which("git")))
    length(system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)) > 0 else NA,
  article_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(article_source)),
  R_seed = 11,
  cells_retained = ncol(pancreas_sub),
  genes_in_active_assay = nrow(pancreas_sub),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

What to Report

A compact differential and enrichment report should include:

  • the grouping column, contrast, and DE method;
  • whether the test is single-cell marker detection, sample-level pseudobulk, or bulk-style differential testing;
  • thresholds for log fold change, adjusted p value, and marker filtering;
  • the gene-set database, species, and enrichment method;
  • the exact srt@tools result names used for downstream plots;
  • pathway interpretations separated from the gene-level DE evidence.

Use enrichment to summarize marker lists or ranked statistics. Do not treat an enriched term as proof that every gene in the pathway changes coherently.
